text: Before sowing, seed producers use two hand techniques to check and improve seed quality. Germination pre-test (ការធ្វើដំណុះសាក): take samples from three points in the seed lot - top, middle, and bottom of the pile or sack - about 100 seeds by hand-count from each point, mix them together, and divide into 5 sub-samples. Place the counted seed in a bowl or jar, add water until it covers the seed by about 3 cm, stir well, and keep the container somewhere warm and safe. After three days, count how many seeds have germinated versus not - the number that sprouted is the germination rate, and this rate is used to work out how much seed needs to be sown to get the desired seedling stand. Salt-water floating selection (ការជ្រើសរើសយកគ្រាប់ពូជទៅសាប): first sun-dry the seed for 2-3 hours to help release it from dormancy, then let it cool. Fill a jar or basin about two-thirds full of water and place a fresh raw egg (or another marker of similar density) in it; add salt gradually while stirring until the egg just floats to the surface - this signals the water has reached the right salinity for sorting healthy, well-filled seed from light or hollow grain. Pour the rice seed into the middle of the jar and stir thoroughly, then skim off and discard any floating empty husks, weak grain, or weed seed. Scoop out the seed that sinks to the bottom (the heavier, better-filled, more viable grain) into a separate container, repeating for the whole lot. Afterward, rinse the salt water off the selected seed thoroughly before storing or sowing it - leftover salt residue can harm germination if not washed away.
